title: The adjunction $f^*\dashv f_*$ on module objects
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and $f\colon X\to Y$ a morphism of
schemes, and let $u\colon\Lambda_Y\to f^{\Ab}_*f^*_{\Ab}\Lambda_Y$ be the unit of
$f^*_{\Ab}\dashv f^{\Ab}_*$. The pullback $f^*$ of [def-sfb-module-upper-star] is left
adjoint to the pushforward $f_*$ of [def-sfb-module-lower-star], by the adjunction
obtained by composing

- the lift $\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\Ab})\dashv
  \operatorname{Res}_u\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(f^{\Ab}_*)$ of the monoidal adjunction
  $f^*_{\Ab}\dashv f^{\Ab}_*$ to module objects ([sk-def-sfb-transport]), and
- the adjunction $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\dashv\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_f}$
  ([sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]),

and transporting the right adjoint along the isomorphism

$$
\operatorname{Res}_u\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(f^{\Ab}_*)\circ\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_f}
\cong f_* .
$$

Concretely, a $\Lambda_X$-linear map $\Lambda_X\otimes_{f^*\Lambda_Y}f^*_{\Ab}M\to N$
is the same as an $f^*\Lambda_Y$-linear map $f^*_{\Ab}M\to N$, which is the same as a
$\Lambda_Y$-linear map $M\to f_*N$.

proof.text: Put $F=f^*_{\Ab}$, $G=f^{\Ab}_*$, $R=\Lambda_Y$, $S=\Lambda_X$, and $\alpha=\alpha_f\colon FR\to S$. The adjunction $F\dashv G$ on abelian sheaves is [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction]; with its stated strong/lax monoidal structures it is monoidal by [lem-sfb-finite-monoidal-adjunction]. Apply [def-sfb-modobj-transport-adjunction] to this adjunction and the monoid $R$. It gives a monoid morphism $u\colon R\to GFR$ and a natural bijection $B_{M,P}\colon\operatorname{Hom}_{FR}(FM,P)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,LP)$, where $L=\operatorname{Res}_u\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(G)$ and $P$ is any $FR$-module. By [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms], $\alpha$ is an isomorphism of ring objects and $\eta_f=G\alpha\circ u$.

source.place: Proof, opening sentence: lift the monoidal adjunction; final sentence: the mate relation

proof.text: Use the extension of scalars already appearing in the definition [def-sfb-module-upper-star], so $f^*M=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha}(FM)=S\otimes_{FR}FM$. Applying [def-sfb-modobj-extend-restrict-adjunction] to $\alpha\colon FR\to S$ gives a natural bijection $A_{M,N}\colon\operatorname{Hom}_S(f^*M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{FR}(FM,\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha}N)$. Explicitly it sends $h$ to $\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha}(h)\circ u_{FM}$, with $u_{FM}$ the extension-of-scalars unit in that cited statement. The source ring $FR$ is commutative: $S$ is commutative by [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and $\alpha$ is a ring isomorphism by step 1. Explicitly, $\alpha\circ\mu_{FR}=\mu_S\circ(\alpha\otimes\alpha)=\mu_S\circ\tau_{S,S}\circ(\alpha\otimes\alpha)=\mu_S\circ(\alpha\otimes\alpha)\circ\tau_{FR,FR}=\alpha\circ\mu_{FR}\circ\tau_{FR,FR}$, using commutativity of $S$ and naturality of the symmetry $\tau$; cancel the isomorphism $\alpha$. The tensor product on the abelian sheaf categories is the symmetric monoidal, colimit-preserving tensor of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]; these are the scalar-extension functors used in the given definition of $f^*$.

source.place: Statement, the extension/restriction adjunction bullet and final concrete Hom correspondence

proof.text:
For an $S$-module $N$ with action $\gamma_N$, expand the actions using [def-sfb-modobj-transport] and [def-sfb-modobj-restriction]. The underlying object of $L(\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha}N)$ is $GN$, and its $R$-action is
$$
G\gamma_N\circ G(\alpha\otimes1_N)\circ\mu^G_{FR,N}\circ(u\otimes1_{GN})
=G\gamma_N\circ\mu^G_{S,N}\circ(G\alpha\otimes1_{GN})\circ(u\otimes1_{GN})
=G\gamma_N\circ\mu^G_{S,N}\circ((G\alpha\circ u)\otimes1_{GN}).
$$
The first equality is naturality of the lax monoidal structure map $\mu^G$ in its first variable, and the second is functoriality of tensor. Substituting $G\alpha\circ u=\eta_f$ from [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] gives exactly the action in [def-sfb-module-lower-star]. On a module morphism $h$, both functors act as $Gh$. Thus the identity on $GN$ is an $R$-linear isomorphism, natural in $N$, giving $i\colon L\circ\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha}\cong f_*$. This calculation also explicitly proves the transport/restriction compatibility and composition of restrictions used in the blueprint; neither is taken as an uncited theorem.

source.place: Proof, displayed transport/restriction isomorphism and composition of restrictions

proof.text:
For $M\in\operatorname{Mod}_R$ and $N\in\operatorname{Mod}_S$, define
$$
\Phi_{M,N}(h)=i_N\circ B_{M,\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha}N}(A_{M,N}(h)).
$$
This is a bijection: its inverse sends $k\colon M\to f_*N$ to $A_{M,N}^{-1}(B_{M,\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha}N}^{-1}(i_N^{-1}\circ k))$. Naturality in $M$ follows from naturality of $A$ and $B$ under precomposition; naturality in $N$ follows from their naturality under postcomposition together with $i_{N'}\circ L(\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha}h)=f_*h\circ i_N$. Hence these natural Hom-bijections define the required adjunction $f^*\dashv f_*$. By construction its bijection is the composite of the extension/restriction and lifted monoidal-adjunction bijections, followed by the identity-underlying-sheaf isomorphism of step 3. It therefore is precisely the transported composite adjunction specified in the statement, and its two stages give the stated concrete correspondence of linear maps.
